questions.question: What is Peterson’s Solution used for?

explanations.a: Memory allocation involves assigning memory to processes, not synchronizing them.
explanations.b: Peterson’s Solution is a software-based process synchronization algorithm used for achieving mutual exclusion in concurrent programming.
explanations.c: Disk scheduling determines the order of disk I/O requests, not process synchronization.
explanations.d: File management involves handling files, not process synchronization.

questions.question: How many processes can Peterson’s Solution handle?

explanations.a: Peterson’s Solution is designed for two processes, not one.
explanations.b: Peterson’s Solution works only for two processes that need to access a shared resource.
explanations.c: It does not support more than two processes simultaneously.
explanations.d: Peterson’s Solution is not scalable to more than two processes.

questions.question: What type of problem does Peterson’s Solution solve?

explanations.a: Deadlock detection is about identifying deadlocks, not preventing them through synchronization.
explanations.b: Peterson’s Solution ensures that only one process enters its critical section at a time, maintaining mutual exclusion.
explanations.c: CPU scheduling is about determining which process runs next, not about mutual exclusion.
explanations.d: Buffer overflow occurs when data exceeds the storage buffer capacity, not a synchronization issue.

questions.question: What is the main condition to achieve mutual exclusion?

answers.a: Both processes must enter the critical section simultaneously
answers.b: Only one process can enter the critical section at a time
answers.d: Any number of processes can enter the critical section

explanations.a: If both processes enter simultaneously, mutual exclusion is violated.
explanations.b: Mutual exclusion ensures that only one process accesses the critical section at a time.
explanations.c: Indefinite waiting causes starvation, not mutual exclusion.
explanations.d: Allowing multiple processes in the critical section violates mutual exclusion.

questions.question: What is the key mechanism used in Peterson’s Solution?

explanations.a: Paging manages memory allocation, not process synchronization.
explanations.b: Virtual memory provides an abstraction of memory, unrelated to mutual exclusion.
explanations.c: Peterson’s Solution relies on two flags and a turn variable to control access to the critical section.
explanations.d: Disk scheduling handles I/O operations, not process synchronization.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'turn' variable in Peterson’s Solution?

answers.a: To indicate which process should enter the critical section next

explanations.a: The turn variable ensures that processes take turns accessing the critical section, preventing race conditions.
explanations.b: The turn variable does not control memory allocation.
explanations.c: Starvation prevention requires fair scheduling, not just a turn variable.
explanations.d: CPU scheduling determines which process runs next, not critical section access.

questions.question: What problem does Peterson’s Solution prevent?

explanations.a: Memory leaks are caused by poor memory management, not lack of mutual exclusion.
explanations.b: Peterson’s Solution prevents race conditions by ensuring only one process accesses the critical section at a time.
explanations.c: Fragmentation is a memory allocation problem, not a synchronization issue.
explanations.d: Deadlocks in distributed systems require more complex handling than Peterson’s Solution.

questions.question: In what type of system is Peterson’s Solution commonly used?

explanations.a: Peterson’s Solution is not suitable for multi-core processors due to modern CPU optimizations.
explanations.b: Single-threaded applications do not require synchronization.
explanations.c: Peterson’s Solution is not typically used in real-time systems.
explanations.d: Peterson’s Solution is designed specifically for two processes.
